name: dispersion_reversal
idea_and_source: One-day cross-sectional reversal only after high-dispersion days: long the day's bottom decile, short the top decile of the point-in-time top-100 list when the day's cross-sectional std is above the q-quantile of the previous 250 days; fill next open, hold 1-3 days, 0.05% a side. Tuned q x hold (12 settings) on 2017-2021; chosen q 0.8, hold 3. source: shelf #1 (Lehmann 1990 / Jegadeesh 1990 reversal; dispersion claim from the moondevonyt notes). Wednesday even-week track (daily strategies); the learning findings were single-day slices and pointed nowhere else.
status: REJECTED (gate REJECT; failed: oos_mean>0_and_P>=0.9, dsr>=0.9, cpcv_pass, edge_reviewer_PASS). read_first: data quality 98 stocks, worst archive coverage 1.00 over 2,737 days; 310 held-out baskets (one result per signal day, not too few); profit factor 0.80 (not suspicious); neighbours hold (chosen tuning Sharpe 0.41, neighbour median 0.27). Held-out P(mean>0) 0.07, DSR 0.001; CPCV median path Sharpe -0.54, 0 of 9 paths positive, PBO 0.49. Checks of the shelf claim: on tuning data the result rose with the dispersion cut (as claimed), but on 2022 onwards every one of the 12 settings lost after costs, and even before costs the unfiltered reversal (+0.023% a basket) beat the high-dispersion one (-0.060%): both contradiction tests in the shelf entry are met. Re-test on data/pit bars with departed names (744 stocks): held-out +0.012% a basket, Sharpe 0.03, so the verdict does not depend on the stock list. Limits: no borrow fee; one spin-off day (RTX 2020-04-03) left unadjusted. backtest-expert score 56/100, decision REJECT (negative expectancy). Trials: 12.

name: L5_breadth_filter
idea_and_source: IMPROVE A BASELINE: L5 RSI(2) pullback on SPY/QQQ/IWM/DIA with one change, an entry filter: take the signal only if at least 30% of the point-in-time top-100 list is above its 20-day average on the signal day (window 20/50 x threshold 30/40/50 tuned on 2016-2021). Reason: this week's learning (ML top feature nh_nl; baseline did best after breadth recovered; L5's largest losses were dips bought in weak breadth). source: own

Gate: held-out mean +0.40% a trade, P(>0) 0.996, DSR 0.882, CPCV median path Sharpe 0.29 with 9 of 9 paths positive but PBO 0.64 (fail). Checklist: double costs +0.30% a trade; VIX terciles low +0.13% (45), mid +0.39% (47), high +0.65% (48); years 2022 +0.74 (5), 2023 +0.18 (23), 2024 +0.67 (41), 2025 +0.22 (27), 2026 +0.33 (44); worst 20 days sum -20.4% of sleeve (worst 2024-12-18 -1.76%); max drawdown 4.8% of sleeve; no look-ahead (signal on the close, breadth from closes to that day, fill next open); ETFs only are traded. The 38 original entries the filter skipped earned +0.23% on average, so the filter removed winners. backtest-expert score 65/100 (VALIDATION_REQUIRED: under 5 held-out years). Why it should have worked: dip buyers are paid by sellers who need to leave now, less so when selling is general; the data did not support it. 6 settings tried (TRIALS).
